newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE CONFIRM IMPROVEMENT WITH 3-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE CONFIRM IMPROVEMENT WITH 3-0 WIN.

text.p: Marseille, looking to regain past glories under a new chairman, beat Auxerre 3-0 in the French first division on Sunday -- their second victory over the European Cup quarter-finalists in six days.

Former French international Xavier Gravelaine put the 1993 European champions on course with a 39th minute goal, then fellow striker Marc Libbra and left back Hamada Jambay sealed the victory with two more in the last seven minutes.
Marseille, the only French side to have won the European Cup, also beat Auxerre 3-2 to put them out of the League Cup on Tuesday.
Auxerre remain fifth in the standings, while Marseille climb from 13th to 10th, 15 points adrift of leaders Monaco after extending their unbeaten run in the league to seven matches.
It was Marseille's first match under new chairman Robert Louis-Dreyfus, who officially took over the club on Friday.
Gravelaine opened the scoring after taking a through ball from midfielder Eric Roy and slipping past Christian Henna into the penalty box on the left.
The striker shot diagonally across goal just before Franck Silvestre's lunging tackle to slot the ball inside the far post beyond the diving Fabien Cool for his sixth goal of the season.

Marseille survived Auxerre's push for an equaliser in the second half, then hit them on the break through Libbra who looked marginally offside when he ran on to Italian defender Alberto Malusci's ball.
Jambay surged past defender Frederic Danjou on to a pass by substitute Ludovic Asuar to shoot past Cool from the left three minutes later.
